svg.text: danielgarcia.it: from a commit to production
the code of the site, and what describes its build
the pages, their data, the layout
generates the site, then serves it
Builds the image from the folder.
Merge develop into main, then push:
The one gesture of a release. Everything below happens on its own.
git push on the main branch
its machines test the site, build the image and publish it
ubuntu-latest virtual machine, created then destroyed
Job test: the site, before any build
copies the repository onto the machine
installs Temurin 25, with the Maven cache
5 tests, internal links included; a failure stops all
Job build, if the tests pass
signs in to the registry (not on pull requests)
works out the tags of the image
builds the image: SKIP_TESTS=true, pull: true
Nginx and the generated pages, nothing else.
the most recent image of main
fetched by the server, without credentials
The server comes to get it: GitHub never connects to the server.
it updates itself, and never builds
two files, on the server only
odd minutes: never at the same
time as the other site's update
downloaded from main after a review
Nginx: the pages, the 404s, the headers
proxy network: reached by the reverse
proxy, which ends HTTPS and sets HSTS
serves the new version a few minutes after the publication.
Numbers follow the order of the steps. Yellow boxes: the two gestures made by hand; everything else
runs on its own. The image is built on the development machine to test, and on GitHub to publish: never on the server.
